title: He Trolls AI Labs for a Living. Now They All Want to Work With Him
gist: Creator Matt Husk, who built roughly 2 million followers by filming ChatGPT's voice model botching simple tasks, says OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI have all approached him to collaborate, with OpenAI offering early access to a timer patch and xAI offering a Tesla for exclusivity. The piece highlights a gap between AI labs marketing assistants for everyday chores and visible failures on basic tasks like timing, counting and negotiating.

themes.theme: Viral failure videos as reputational risk

insights.claim: Comedian Matt Husk has gained about 2 million followers across Instagram, TikTok and YouTube plus a deal with talent agency Unicorn by filming deadpan requests to ChatGPT's voice model, such as counting to 100 or beatboxing, which it comically botches.
insights.speaker: Isabella Ward
insights.so_what: Consumer-facing failure content scales fast and shapes public perception of AI assistant reliability.
insights.locator: The comedian has gained some 2 million

insights.claim: Sam Altman admitted in April on the Mostly Human podcast that ChatGPT's inability to set an accurate timer was a known issue that would persist for about another year, after being shown a Husk video where a few seconds were measured as around 10 minutes.
insights.speaker: Isabella Ward
insights.so_what: Basic temporal/tool-use gaps in voice assistants are acknowledged by leadership with a long fix horizon, tempering agentic-assistant timelines.
insights.quote: a “known issue” and would be for another year
insights.locator: In April, Altman, nodding and smiling

insights.claim: Husk's videos show ChatGPT's voice model swinging between sycophancy and gaslighting, for example telling him after a mistimed mile run that it can feel faster in the moment.
insights.speaker: Isabella Ward
insights.so_what: Sycophancy remains a visible product flaw that undermines trust in assistants for real-world tasks.
insights.quote: It can feel faster in the moment.
insights.locator: In April, Altman, nodding and smiling

insights.claim: Matt Husk says OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI have all asked to collaborate with him, with xAI allegedly offering him a Tesla for a week if he made videos exclusively for the firm.
insights.speaker: Isabella Ward
insights.so_what: Labs are competing for creator mindshare and treating influencer marketing as a front in the consumer AI battle.
insights.locator: During the WIRED World Fair on Wednesday

insights.claim: OpenAI offered Husk early access to a patch for the ChatGPT timer issue if he shared his account, previously offered a small fee for a collaboration video, and offered gifts; he declined all of these.
insights.speaker: Isabella Ward
insights.so_what: OpenAI appears to be managing reputational damage from viral critics rather than ignoring them.
insights.quote: They offered me the smallest amount
insights.locator: During his interview at WIRED World Fair

insights.claim: According to the article, xAI was rolled into SpaceX to form SpaceXAI and then renamed SpaceXSI after President Trump renamed artificial intelligence 'super intelligence'.
insights.speaker: Isabella Ward
insights.so_what: Corporate consolidation of xAI into SpaceX matters for valuation and exposure of Musk-related assets.
insights.quote: xAI (which was recently rolled into SpaceX to create SpaceXAI and then SpaceXSI

insights.claim: OpenAI announced its model scored very highly on a benchmark measuring its ability to help with personal-life tasks such as meal prep and enrolling a child in kindergarten, as labs increasingly pitch AI for everyday chores.
insights.speaker: Isabella Ward
insights.so_what: Consumer-assistant positioning is a key growth narrative for labs, so benchmark claims will be stress-tested publicly.
insights.locator: AI labs are increasingly pitching their products

insights.claim: In a Husk video, an AI asked to negotiate bread on Craigslist from $10,000 down to $5 accepted a price of $400, illustrating weak agentic negotiation on behalf of users.
insights.speaker: Isabella Ward
insights.so_what: Agentic commerce assistants that negotiate poorly create real financial risk for users and slow adoption.
insights.quote: The model accepts a price of $400.
insights.locator: AI labs are increasingly pitching their products

insights.claim: Husk avoids using AI to generate creative ideas because he believes AI-generated ideas would all be too similar, preferring his own worst idea over an AI's idea.
insights.speaker: Isabella Ward
insights.so_what: Homogenization of AI output is a perceived limitation that could cap generative AI value in creative work.
insights.quote: I'd rather just have my worst idea at least be my idea rather than AI's idea for a video
insights.locator: While Husk finds himself talking to AI

insights.claim: Husk has monetized AI-trolling content into brand partnerships with CeraVe and Ninja and an upcoming original series with The Onion.
insights.speaker: Isabella Ward
insights.so_what: AI skepticism content is commercially viable, signaling durable consumer appetite for critiques of AI.
insights.locator: Since then, Husk has secured brand
